yarn-troppo.meaning: Every beat survives: the widow, the $6,000, the ad verbatim, Andy's mermaid line, Zeke's wrong bottle. Additions hang off the original: "Wrong bottle, poor bugger.", "rest his soul", "and that's the whole box and dice gone", "sticky fingers and all". "you can't trust 'em as far as you can throw 'em" overstates "not trustworthy" a little.
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "lurk" for graft, "shonky little raids" for illegitimate inroads, "council by-laws" for city ordinances, "staying back at the office" for working overtime, "on the take" for grafting is close enough. "put his noggin back together" for reconstructing his mind works.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Natural Australian voice: "fed up to the back teeth", "a good hard squiz", "strife with the cops", "the whole box and dice", "got sloshed on". A few lines feel added for flavour, e.g. "sticky fingers and all".
yarn-troppo.register: A solid level 3, leaning toward 4 with the extra idiom ("whole box and dice", "comes sniffing round", "he goes"). Vulgarity within 1: "poor bugger".
yarn-troppo.tone: Keeps Jeff's mock-learned con-man drawl: "perfidiousness", "So far, so pernicious", "hereditaments and appurtenances" all kept, and the deadpan of "Why's there gotta be a lady?"
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads well aloud; one pile-up in "five nippers, sticky fingers and all, and a building and loan mortgage" and the split "Dead calm on top, and fed up to the back teeth underneath." is slightly laboured.
yarn-troppo.variety: Good spread, though "lurk" and "racket" each recur and "cooked up"/"cooking up" repeat: "marriage agency lurk we cooked up", "cooking up our little masterpiece".
yarn-troppo.essence: Unmistakably O. Henry's Jeff Peters: the paradox of the honest sex, the ad, the rule that the goods must be producible, the widow of Zeke.

dinkum-3.meaning: Story intact, but the ad is paraphrased into plain modern English ("Doesn't mind an older man or a plain-looking one", "Write, with particulars") and "wasn't hard on the eye" says she was attractive, against "except maybe for beauty".
dinkum-3.sense: "how sneaky women are" literalises "perfidiousness" and loses the joke that Jeff is complaining they aren't crooked; "wasn't hard on the eye" takes the wrong sense of "feasible and praiseworthy to the eye". "off-siders" and "a swifty" fit well.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Mostly natural: "off-siders", "a bit of a swifty", "building society mortgage", "fronting a justice of the peace", "pop in at their place". Sounds like a local.
dinkum-3.register: Level 3 about right; vulgarity 1 used once, "no bloody marriage in it". Slightly heavier than needed by also rewriting the ad.
dinkum-3.tone: Flattens some of the mock-learned style: "Whenever I'm bending the letter of the law, the goods I'm selling have to be real" loses "existent, visible, producible". Ad loses its period stiffness.
dinkum-3.flow: Smooth and readable throughout: "Andy gives me one of his looks, calm but fed up."
dinkum-3.variety: "lurk" leans hard: "marriage agency lurk", "a lurk like ours", "to work this lurk", "a marriage lurk".
dinkum-3.essence: Recognisably the story, but the ad rewrite and the plainer legal pastiche flatten what makes it O. Henry.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point kept, nothing invented; the ad left verbatim apart from spelling ("realises"). "say a roll as fat as the little end of a wagon tongue" keeps the image.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Every term fits: "put much stock in", "the most innocent sort of lurk", "the other lot either on the take", "shonky raids on the letter of the law", "council by-laws", "decent enough to the eye".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural, understated Australian: "knocked up an ad", "chucked in them ideas", "comes sniffing round", "an old mate of mine", "got sloshed on". Nothing stagey.
yarn-dinkum.register: A light level 3; perhaps a touch under, keeping "said I" and "finds her" and adding few terms beyond "bloke", "nippers", "dosh", "flog", "cops". No swearing, which vulgarity 1 permits.
yarn-dinkum.tone: The arch narrator survives whole: "the article sold has got to exist, be seen and be produced", "So far, so pernicious".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Andy gives me one of his calm, fed-up looks."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Terms are spread out with little repetition; "scheme" recurs but follows the original.

engine.meaning: Mostly the original text untouched, but swaps inside the quoted ad change it: "possessing $3,000 dosh", "elderly bloke", "invest dosh with judgment". "Bloody hell, we had about $6,000" adds an exclamation.
engine.sense: "dosh" and "bloke" inside a formal newspaper ad strain badly; "Bugger me, but where" and "Bloody hell" are misplaced emphasis.
engine.authenticity: Stage-Australian: swears bolted onto untranslated Edwardian prose, "too bloody much", "as bloody big as", "reconstructing his bloody mind", "our bloody agency".
engine.register: Mostly untranslated (keeps "I never had much confidence in the perfidiousness of woman", "'Twas only sixty miles"), so far under level 3 in Aussie, while swearing is crammed in at a density that feels over the dad brief.
engine.tone: The swears jar against the arch style, e.g. "Bloody hell, we had about $6,000", making the narrator sound agitated rather than urbane.
engine.flow: Jarring joins: "Bloody hell, we had about $6,000 and we expected to double it", "Bugger me, but where,' he says".
engine.variety: Leans on the same few insertions: "bloody" five times, "dosh" three times.
engine.essence: The original text is mostly there, so the story is recognisable, but the swears distort the voice.

unharnessed.meaning: Story intact. "where's the sheila?" and "an actual woman" keep the point; "flogging themselves on overtime" keeps working overtime. "in a travelling tent show" is a harmless gloss.
unharnessed.sense: Mostly fits, but "their hairdos get worked up too much" loses "hair touched up" (dyed) and garbles it, and "right as rain in business" strains for "all right in business". "running lurks" for grafting is good.
unharnessed.authenticity: Largely natural: "there's a quid to be made", "a good hard squiz", "front up with", "given away them ideas", "pretty bloody well". Leaves US "realizes" in the ad.
unharnessed.register: Level 3 on the nose, with one dad-level "pretty bloody well".
unharnessed.tone: The mock-learned voice kept: "the looks, hereditaments and appurtenances", "So far, so pernicious".
unharnessed.flow: Mostly smooth; one awkward stretch, "Fair enough, they've earned that one,' I said", mixes I said with the I says used later.
unharnessed.variety: "caper" leaned on: "marriage agency caper", "a caper like ours", "a marriage caper", plus "gotta" three times.

yarn-troppo.original: or hereafter be held by a justice of the peace.

dinkum-3.quote: I never had much faith in how sneaky women are
dinkum-3.original: I never had much confidence in the perfidiousness of woman
dinkum-3.why: Turns Jeff's comic misuse into a plain statement, losing the paradox that sets up the honest sex.

dinkum-3.original: she looked feasible and praiseworthy to the eye
dinkum-3.why: Says she was good-looking, contradicting the line just before (except maybe for beauty).

dinkum-3.quote: Doesn't mind an older man or a plain-looking one
dinkum-3.original: No objection to elderly man or one of homely appearance
dinkum-3.why: The ad is a quoted document in a stiff period style; modernising it loses its flavour.
Fourth use of lurk; leaned on.

yarn-dinkum.quote: five nippers and a building and loan mortgage
yarn-dinkum.original: five kids and a building and loan mortgage
yarn-dinkum.why: Keeps the American building and loan; building society would read more local.

summaries.yarn-troppo: Lively, natural Aussie retelling that keeps the whole story and its learned con-man voice; a few bolted-on asides.
summaries.dinkum-3: Fluent and authentic, but rewrites the ad, loses the perfidiousness joke and gets Mrs Trotter's looks backwards.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Faithful, clean and natural; a measured level 3 that keeps every point and the original's voice.
summaries.engine: Rule-engine output: largely untranslated, with bloody and dosh dropped in, even into the quoted ad.
summaries.unharnessed: Natural level-3 retelling that keeps story and tone; leans on caper and leaves a US spelling.
